szoveg_eredeti:
The UNESCO Regional Office in Santiago commemorated the 25th anniversary of the Information for All Programme (IFAP) with two regional events held in Montevideo and Santiago. The activities brought together specialists from Latin America and the Caribbean to reflect on the challenges posed by artificial intelligence (AI) for education, media and information literacy, and information integrity.

Both events were held within the framework of a UNESCO Santiago initiative that was selected to receive international funding from the IFAP Programme in 2026. The proposal was one of three initiatives supported by the Programme worldwide that year, alongside projects from West Africa and the Caribbean.

Implemented through UNESCO’s Observatory on Artificial Intelligence in Education for Latin America and the Caribbean, the project seeks to strengthen critical artificial intelligence literacy among teachers, students and education authorities by promoting the capacities needed to understand, evaluate and use these technologies ethically, critically and responsibly.

Over these 25 years, the relevance of IFAP has been closely linked to a challenge that directly affects everyday life: ensuring that people are not only able to access information, but also have the tools needed to understand it, assess its reliability and use it to make informed decisions. From recognizing misleading content on social media to harnessing the opportunities offered by artificial intelligence for learning and work, these capacities are increasingly important for navigating a digital society with autonomy.

“The Information for All Programme reminds us that ensuring access to information also means developing the capacities needed to understand, evaluate and use it critically. At UNESCO Santiago, we are advancing this work in Latin America and the Caribbean, particularly in response to the challenges and opportunities that artificial intelligence presents for education and for building more inclusive knowledge societies,” said Esther Kuisch Laroche, Director of the UNESCO Regional Office in Santiago.

The event, entitled “Critical literacy in the age of artificial intelligence: capacities to understand, evaluate and act in AI-mediated environments”, was held on 15 October at the MERCOSUR Building, in collaboration with the Ministry of Education and Culture of Uruguay, as part of EduIA Conf 2026.

The event brought together specialists from Chile, Argentina and Uruguay to reflect on the transformations that artificial intelligence is bringing to education processes, access to information and knowledge production.

Opening remarks were delivered by Valtencir M. Mendes, Head of Education at UNESCO Santiago, and Andrea Vignolo Mosca, Director of International Cooperation and Projects at Uruguay’s Ministry of Education and Culture.

The event featured contributions from Rayén Condeza Dall’Orso, from the UNESCO-UC Chair on Media and Information Literacy in Digital Spaces at the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile; Roxana Morduchowicz, PhD in Communication and UNESCO Senior Adviser on Digital Citizenship; and Javiera Sánchez Ríos, from Ceibal’s Training and Pedagogical Innovation Department in Uruguay.

The dialogue highlighted that artificial intelligence literacy must go beyond the technical use of tools and include competencies for critically evaluating information, identifying bias, recognizing misinformation risks, and understanding the ethical and privacy implications associated with these technologies.

The event also addressed the importance of integrating media and information literacy into teacher education, education systems and public policies, promoting a citizenry capable of navigating digital environments autonomously, critically and responsibly.

The regional commemoration continued on 26 October in the Chilean capital with the event “Critical literacy in the age of artificial intelligence: understanding, evaluating and taking action”, co-organized with Universidad Alberto Hurtado (UAH) as part of the university’s Second Artificial Intelligence Week and Global Media and Information Literacy Week (MIL).

One of the central moments was the keynote address “Information integrity as a public good”, delivered by Guilherme Canela, Director of UNESCO’s Section for Digital Policies and Digital Transformation in Paris and Secretary of the IFAP Programme.

During his presentation, Canela addressed the challenges associated with misinformation, artificial intelligence and the transformation of information ecosystems, highlighting the need to strengthen critical thinking and promote trustworthy information environments.

The event also featured Valtencir M. Mendes, Head of Education at UNESCO Santiago, as well as specialists from Chile, Argentina and Colombia, including Marcos Mendiburu, Alejandra Falabella, María Teresa Rojas, Tomás Durán and Francisco Fernández.

The discussions focused on the importance of media and information literacy as a tool for addressing the challenges of digital transformation, strengthening citizens’ capacities and contributing to the integrity of information ecosystems.

This article is related to the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goals.
